facts.text: Queen's University is Kingston's largest employer with 9,352 employees, followed by Kingston Health Sciences Centre with 5,953 and Canadian Forces Base Kingston with 5,800.
Queen's University contributes $1.67 billion in GDP and 14,946 jobs to Kingston, and 1 in 10 jobs in the city are found at Queen's.
In 2024 Kingston welcomed 2.6 million visitors who spent $512 million, and tourism generated $775 million of economic activity in the city.

overview: Kingston had 132,485 residents in the 2021 Census, up 7.0% from 123,798 in 2016. The median age is 41.2 and the median household income in 2020 was $79,000. Its 57,836 occupied dwellings are spread across 451.58 square kilometres, so the customer base is wide as well as growing.

Queen's University, Kingston Health Sciences Centre and CFB Kingston anchor employment, and 2.6 million visitors arrive each year. A local business serves steady institutional households plus a large seasonal tourist market.
